title: Volume and Page Numbering for Separate Note Volumes

illustrates.quote: The following is an example of the volume and page numbering for the individual volumes. The text is in the first volume, with notes in the following volume.

blocks.text:
Volume 3
Braille pages t1-t5 and 1-67
Print pages 45-a70

Volume 4
Braille pages t1-t5 and 1-55
Print pages 45-a70
blocks.features: Plain indented text listing, for two consecutive volumes, their own braille page ranges (each with its own preliminary-pages t1-t5 sequence) against the same shared print page range (45-a70), since Volume 4 holds the notes for the text in Volume 3.

print.surroundingText: Follows rule 16.7.7b, illustrating the combined-page-numbering scheme described in 16.7.7a for a text volume and its separate notes volume.
print.printFeatures: Plain indented text list, no box; two short volume/page-range blocks separated by a blank line. Purely descriptive numbering information, not itself a braille-transcribed passage.

braille.notes: This is a description of a volume/page-numbering scheme (plain print numerals), not a passage transcribed into braille; the source shows no corresponding braille rendering. None is guessed here.

uncertain: No braille rendering exists for this item in the source; it documents a numbering scheme rather than transcribing print text.
resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.7.b per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: print-only per standards-map.md; both runs agree. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
